what.label: supported
what.says: The Trevi Fountain was designed by Nicola Salvi and completed by Giuseppe Pannini in 1762; at 26.3 metres (86 ft) high and 49.15 metres (161.3 ft) wide it is the largest Baroque fountain in the world.
quote: designed by Italian architect Nicola Salvi and completed by Giuseppe Pannini in 1762. Standing 26.3 metres (86 ft) high and 49.15 metres (161.3 ft) wide, it is the largest Baroque fountain in the world

tucked.label: supported
tucked.says: Visitors are amazed that such a big fountain is tucked into a small square among side streets.
quote: Visitors are always amazed that such a big and famous fountain is tucked away in a small piazza in the middle of side streets.

pickpockets.label: supported
pickpockets.says: The Trevi Fountain area is well known for pickpockets.
quote: and the Trevi fountain are well known for pickpockets, so take extra care in these areas.

ticket.label: supported
ticket.says: Non-residents now usually need a 2-euro ticket to approach the fountain and throw coins in during the day; after 10 p.m. the barriers open.
quote: On 2 February 2026, the City Council of Rome introduced a ticketing system where non-residents will need to buy a 2-euro ticket to approach the fountain and throw coins into its waters
After 10 p.m., the barriers are opened and access is free for all.
the Trevi fountain costs €2

name.label: supported
name.says: The name comes from trivium, the meeting of three streets.
quote: The name of the fountain derives from the Latin word trivium, meaning "intersection of three streets".

aqueduct.label: supported
aqueduct.says: The fountain is the end of the Acqua Vergine, the revived ancient Aqua Virgo aqueduct of 19 BC, which still carries water here.
quote: marks the terminal point of the "modern" Acqua Vergine—the revived Aqua Virgo, one of the aqueducts that supplied water to ancient Rome.
In 19 BC, supposedly with the help of a virgin, Roman technicians located a source of pure water
The aqueduct is still in use today

virgin.label: legend
virgin.says: The story goes that a virgin showed Roman engineers the spring; the scene is on the fountain's façade, in the reliefs above.
quote: supposedly with the help of a virgin, Roman technicians located a source of pure water some 13 km (8.1 mi) from the city. (This scene is presented on the present fountain's façade.)
Above, bas reliefs illustrate the Roman origin of the aqueducts.

oceanus.label: supported
oceanus.says: In the central niche stands Oceanus by Pietro Bracci; tritons guide his shell chariot and tame sea horses.
quote: Pietro Bracci (whose statue of Oceanus sits in the central niche)
Tritons guide Oceanus's shell chariot, taming hippocamps.

flanking.label: supported
flanking.says: In the niches either side of Oceanus, Abundance spills water from her urn and Salubrity, health, holds a cup a snake drinks from.
quote: In the niches flanking Oceanus, Abundance spills water from her urn and Salubrity holds a cup from which a snake drinks.

theme.label: supported
theme.says: The theme is the taming of the waters; the backdrop is the façade of the Palazzo Poli.
quote: The backdrop for the fountain is the Palazzo Poli
Taming of the waters is the theme of the gigantic scheme

bernini.label: supported
bernini.says: In 1629 Pope Urban VIII asked Bernini for designs, but the project was dropped when the pope died.
quote: In 1629, Pope Urban VIII, finding the earlier fountain insufficiently dramatic, asked Gian Lorenzo Bernini to sketch possible renovations, but the project was abandoned when the Pope died.

contest.label: supported
contest.says: In Clement XII's 1730 contest Salvi lost to Alessandro Galilei, but Romans protested a Florentine winning, and Salvi got the job; work began in 1732. Salvi died in 1751 with the work half done.
quote: In 1730, Pope Clement XII organized a contest in which Nicola Salvi initially lost to Alessandro Galilei – but due to the outcry in Rome over a Florentine having won, Salvi was awarded the commission anyway. Work began in 1732.
Salvi died in 1751 with his work half finished

ace.label: supported
ace.says: Salvi hid a barber's ugly sign behind a sculpted vase that Romans call the Ace of Cups.
quote: he had made sure a barber's unsightly sign would not spoil the ensemble, hiding it behind a sculpted vase, called by Romans the asso di coppe, the "Ace of Cups"

coin.label: tradition
coin.says: By tradition, throwing a coin in before leaving Rome means you will return; you throw with your back to the fountain, right hand over the left shoulder.
quote: The best known and most persistent tradition consists of throwing a coin into the fountain before leaving "the eternal city", a superstition associated with the fountain being that whoever makes this gesture would favor a future return to the city. Coins are purportedly meant to be thrown while turning one's back to the fountain, using the right hand over the left shoulder.

money.label: estimate
money.says: An estimated 3,000 euros a day are thrown in, and the money goes to the charity Caritas.
quote: An estimated 3,000 euros are thrown into the fountain each day.
The money thrown into the fountain is donated to the Caritas association, which uses it for charity work

steal.label: supported
steal.says: There are regular attempts to steal the coins, though it is illegal.
quote: there are regular attempts to steal coins from the fountain, although it is illegal to do so.

travertine.label: supported
travertine.says: Most of the fountain is travertine stone quarried near Tivoli, about 35 kilometres (22 miles) east of Rome.
quote: The majority of the piece is made from Travertine stone, quarried near Tivoli, about 35 kilometres (22 miles) east of Rome.

allegories.label: supported
allegories.says: Pannini put the present allegories in place of planned statues of Agrippa and Trivia; Pope Clement XIII opened the fountain on 22 May.
quote: who substituted the present allegories for planned sculptures of Agrippa and Trivia, the Roman virgin. It was officially opened and inaugurated on 22 May by Pope Clement XIII.

restore.label: supported
restore.says: The fashion house Fendi sponsored a 20-month restoration, the most thorough in the fountain's history, finished in November 2015, which added more than 100 LED lights.
quote: In January 2013, it was announced that the Italian fashion company Fendi would sponsor a 20-month, 2.2-million-euro restoration of the fountain, the most thorough in the fountain's history. Restoration work began in June 2014 and was completed in November 2015.
The restoration included the installation of more than 100 LED lights to improve the nighttime illumination of the fountain.

respighi.label: supported
respighi.says: Respighi's 1916 tone poem Fountains of Rome has a movement called The Trevi Fountain at Noon.
quote: The Trevi Fountain is depicted in the third movement, "The Trevi Fountain at Noon", of Ottorino Respighi's 1916 symphonic poem Fountains of Rome.

films.label: supported
films.says: The fountain starred in Roman Holiday and Three Coins in the Fountain, and in La Dolce Vita Anita Ekberg wades into it with Marcello Mastroianni.
quote: including Roman Holiday (1953); Three Coins in the Fountain (1954)
In Federico Fellini's 1960 film La Dolce Vita, Anita Ekberg wades into the fountain with Marcello Mastroianni.

parts.name: Arriving
parts.stand: Come into the little square and find a spot with a clear view of the fountain.

paras.t: And suddenly, there it is: the Trevi Fountain, tucked into this small square among the side streets. It's the largest Baroque fountain in the world, 86 feet high and about 161 feet wide, finished in 1762.
Crowds gather here, and so do pickpockets. Keep your bag zipped and in front of you.
To go down to the water's edge and throw a coin, visitors now usually need a 2-euro ticket during the day; late at night the barriers open. Check on the day.
The name comes from the Latin trivium, the meeting of three streets.

parts.name: Reading the fountain
parts.stand: Stay facing the center of the fountain.

paras.t: The theme is the taming of the waters. In the central niche stands Oceanus, by the sculptor Pietro Bracci, on a shell chariot, with tritons wrestling sea horses below him.
On either side of him are two figures. One is Abundance, pouring water from her urn. The other is Salubrity, health, holding a cup that a snake drinks from.
This water has a long history. The fountain is the end of an aqueduct that goes back to 19 BC, the Aqua Virgo, and it is still in use today.
Look up at the carved panels above: they show how the aqueduct began. Legend has it that a virgin helped Roman engineers find the spring.

parts.name: How it was built
parts.stand: Step a little to one side so you can see the whole width of the palace behind the fountain.

paras.t: The fountain is built right onto the back of a palace, the Palazzo Poli. It took more than a century of tries to get it built.

In 1629 Pope Urban VIII asked Bernini for ideas, but the pope died and the plan was dropped. Then in 1730 there was a contest. Nicola Salvi lost, to a man from Florence, and Romans were so outraged that Salvi got the job anyway. Work began in 1732. Salvi died in 1751 with the fountain half done, and Giuseppe Pannini finished it.

Most of it is travertine, a pale stone quarried near Tivoli, about 22 miles east of Rome. Pannini changed the plan at the end: instead of statues of Agrippa and of Trivia, the Roman virgin, he put in the figures you see now. Pope Clement XIII opened it on May 22, 1762.
A barber's ugly shop sign would have spoiled the effect, so Salvi hid it behind a big sculpted vase. Romans call it the Ace of Cups.

parts.name: The coin
parts.stand: Turn so your back is to the fountain.

paras.t: Now the tradition. Throw a coin into the fountain before you leave Rome, and it's believed you'll come back. You throw it with your back to the water, right hand over your left shoulder.
By one estimate, some 3,000 euros go in every day, and the money is given to the charity Caritas. So your wish helps someone else.
Some people try to fish the coins out. It's illegal, and it happens regularly anyway.

The night lighting owes something to the fashion house Fendi, which paid for a 20-month restoration, the most thorough in the fountain's history. It was finished in November 2015 and added more than 100 LED lights.
And it has its own music. Respighi's 1916 piece Fountains of Rome includes a movement called The Trevi Fountain at Noon.
The fountain is a film star too: in Roman Holiday, in Three Coins in the Fountain, and in La Dolce Vita, where Anita Ekberg wades in with Marcello Mastroianni.

parts.name: Closing
parts.stand: Take one last look before you go.

paras.t: Everyone here is hoping for the same small thing: to come back. Whether or not the coin works, it's a good wish to make.
